result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer B gives all the prices and dates correctly, tells monthly and annual customers separately when the new price applies, and bases its reasons only on the sheet: four years without a change, plus the new bank feeds and mileage tracking. It also explains why it left out the unsupported 'costs went up' claim and offers a line to add if costs really did rise. Answer A is equally clear and short, but it says 'Our costs have gone up,' which is not on the sheet and breaks rubric item 3. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers get the prices, the 1 March date and the separate monthly and annual timing right. They are short and calm. Answer B says 'our costs have gone up', which the fact sheet does not support and rubric item 3 forbids. It also adds an unsupported promise to keep improving the product. Answer A gives only the reasons on the sheet, says plainly why it left out the costs line, and points out that the 'six weeks ahead' wording may not match the actual send date.
